title: Private Session Data Sent to Non-Allowlisted External API

invariant.statement: An agent must not include data classified as private (PII, session secrets, customer records, internal config) in an outbound request whose destination host is not on a fixed allowlist.

claim.statement: If the agent's outbound HTTP tool accepts a caller-supplied URL and the request body is constructed by the LLM (or by another tool that returns user data), an attacker who controls the prompt can name an external destination — `attacker.example`, a webhook collector, a public Pastebin — and the agent will exfiltrate session data to it.

mitigation.summary: Outbound HTTP from the agent goes through a single safePost wrapper that (1) checks the destination host against a fixed allowlist, (2) classifies the request body and rejects bodies containing private-tagged fields when the destination is not on an internal allowlist, (3) logs every outbound call with destination and content-class. Prefer per-tool destination allowlists (e.g., the Stripe tool can only POST to api.stripe.com) over a global one.

references: MITRE ATLAS: AML.T0024 — Exfiltration via API
